lead_1_bell_diagonal_Z4: For Z4-Weyl Bell-diagonal ququart states rho=sum p_x P(Omega_x), Omega_x=(W_x x 1)Omega, W_(a,b)=Z^aX^b: SN<=2 iff p lies in conv{|Tr(W_x^dag A)|^2/(4Tr A^dag A) : rank A<=2} (Weyl spectra of rank-<=2 matrices). Twirling is local-unitary mixing, so both directions hold. PPT iff the four 4x4 matrices M_t(x,x')=phat_{x+x'-t}(x-x') are PSD, where phat_b(m)=sum_a p_(a,b) i^(am). Derivation: rho is block-circulant in Alice-Bob shift sectors; the PT is block-diagonal in Alice+Bob sum sectors. Superposing two Bell states whose labels differ by an order-2 element gives SR2, so mass split 1/2-1/2 inside a coset of H={0,(2,0),(0,2),(2,2)} is SN2. Source check: arXiv 2610.12000 (Patra-Hiesmayr) concerns the PAULI-lattice ququart basis, and its APPT threshold is 'six largest <=1/2' (not 1). So uniform-on-six states are NOT automatically PPT. No Z4 claim is imported.
lead_2_nilpotent_range: Range-criterion design: take A0 invertible (WLOG 1 by local filters) and N a subspace with no element having a nonzero eigenvalue of geometric multiplicity >=2 (e.g. N nilpotent). Then rank(c0*1+B)>=3 for c0!=0, so every SR2 range vector lies in N. Any state with range C*Omega + N would then have SN>=3. In 3x3 this is impossible for PPT states by YLT, consistent with the obstruction below.
written_obstruction: If N is simultaneously strictly upper triangular after a local unitary U x conj(U), which preserves Omega, then NO PPT state has range C*Omega+N. Proof: for j>i, |ji> is orthogonal to the range, so (rho^Gamma)_{ji,ji}=<ji|rho|ji>=0. PSD forces (rho^Gamma)_{ij,ji}=<ii|rho|jj>=0. But the projection of the range onto span{|kk>} is C*Omega, so P_diag rho P_diag=c P(Omega), and c=0 contradicts Omega in the range. Non-triangularizable N, and N with only nonzero simple eigenvalues, remain unexamined.
